taskCatalog.title: Book your movers

researchPrefs.question: What matters most when you choose a mover?
How flexible is your move date?
Which items need the most attention?

taskCatalog.desc: Get binding estimates from three USDOT-licensed movers. Book 8-12 weeks out for summer moves, 4-6 weeks off-season.
taskCatalog.tips: Get a binding estimate — federal law caps your final bill at 110%.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Booking late means leftover dates, leftover crews, and leftover quality.

content.reframe: You're about to hand every company the information that actually sets the price — because they won't ask, and what they don't know shows up as move-day surprises on the bill.
insiderItems: Always get the packing quote included — even if you plan to pack yourself. It's free to quote, and it's leverage and a fallback if packing runs long.
Valuation isn't insurance. The standard coverage is 60 cents per pound — a 10-lb TV pays out $6. If anything you own matters, ask what full-value protection costs before you book.
Specialty items — piano, safe, grandfather clock — carry disassembly and handling fees. Name them on the first call or meet them as surprises on the invoice.
A quote well below the others isn't a deal, it's a hook. Lowball bids grow on move day, when you have no options.
If you have to chase a company for the quote, drop them. Blown follow-through before they have your money doesn't improve after.

say: Volunteer your access info before they ask: stairs, elevator, long walks, how far the truck parks from the door. Hourly crews bill the walk.
Name every specialty item: piano, safe, treadmill, anything oversized.
Tell them you want the packing quote included.
ask: Is pricing port-to-port hourly, or a fixed travel fee?
How do you charge for supplies — percentage, per item, or can I supply my own?
What does full-value protection cost for my move?
What are the fees for specialty items?
get: The quote in writing, with crew size, hourly rate, and travel fee broken out.
Their COI turnaround time if your building needs one.

taskCatalog.title: Book your cleaners

researchPrefs.question: What matters most when you choose a cleaner?
How much cleaning do you need?

taskCatalog.desc: Schedule a move-out deep clean for the day after your movers finish. Get three quotes and confirm scope in writing.
taskCatalog.tips: Insist 'inside appliances' is in writing — most charge extra otherwise.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: One missed area can cost you your entire security deposit.

content.reframe: Say the words 'move-out clean.' A standard clean and a move-out clean are different jobs with different checklists — booking the wrong one means paying twice.

say: Ask for a MOVE-OUT clean, not a standard clean.
Give them your room count and honest condition.
ask: Flat price, not hourly — hourly on a move-out clean is a blank check.
Do you have a re-clean guarantee if the landlord flags something?
get: A receipt — it's your evidence in a deposit dispute.
A slot with a buffer day before key return, never the same day.

taskCatalog.title: Rent your moving truck

researchPrefs.question: What matters most for your truck rental?
How fixed is your pickup time?
What is your main truck concern?

taskCatalog.desc: Compare U-Haul, Penske, and Budget on size, mileage, and total cost. Reserve 4-6 weeks out — earlier in summer.
taskCatalog.tips: Size up if borderline — one trip always beats two.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Late means the wrong size, wrong pickup location, or no truck at all.

content.reframe: The truck size isn't a question — your scan already answered it. The traps are the reservation fine print and the calendar.
insiderItems: Month-end sells out. The 28th through the 3rd is the crunch — everyone's lease turns over at once. If your date lands there, book the moment you know it.
A U-Haul 'reservation' is a request, not a truck. If your date can't move, book with a company that guarantees the actual truck.
Your car insurance and your credit card do NOT cover rental trucks. Take the damage waiver — this is the one upsell that's real.
Photograph the fuel gauge and odometer at pickup and return. That photo is the whole dispute.
Reserve the ramp, dolly, and pads WITH the truck. They sell out separately, and a truck without a ramp is a wall.

taskCatalog.title: Schedule internet install

researchPrefs.question: What matters most for your internet service?
When do you need service working?

taskCatalog.desc: Protect your first workday from an outage: order service 2-3 weeks ahead, confirm exact-address availability, and ask whether self-install is available.
taskCatalog.tips: If your home is pre-wired, compare self-install timing and current fees with a technician appointment.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Without it, you're tethering work calls to your phone for days.

insiderItems: Transferring your current service keeps your existing rate. Moving is also the one window where new-customer pricing opens up — check both before you decide.
Mid-contract? Ask about the early-termination fee before you cancel anything.
Book the install BEFORE you move — slots run 1–2 weeks out. Working from home on day one starts with this call.

taskCatalog.title: Sell what you're not bringing
taskCatalog.desc: List on Facebook Marketplace, OfferUp, or Craigslist 4+ weeks out. Drop the price 10-20% every three days until it sells.
taskCatalog.tips: Post photos in natural daylight — listings sell twice as fast.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Every unsold item becomes a box you pay to move.

content.reframe: Every cubic foot you don't move is money. The window matters: 3–4 weeks out is the SELL window — Marketplace needs time to find buyers.
insiderItems: Inside two weeks, stop selling and switch to donation — charities that pick up furniture free book 1–2 weeks ahead, and the free pickup is the whole trick.

taskCatalog.title: Schedule donation pickup

researchPrefs.question: What matters most for removing these items?
How soon do the items need to go?
What makes up most of the load?

taskCatalog.desc: Book a free pickup with Salvation Army or Habitat ReStore 3-4 weeks out — peak season wait times stretch to a month.
taskCatalog.tips: Get an itemized receipt at pickup — it's a tax write-off.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Last-minute, you'll be hauling furniture to the curb yourself.

content.reframe: The ladder: 1–2 weeks out = donation pickup (book it now — they schedule 1–2 weeks ahead). Final days = junk haul or curb. Movers charge for truck space either way.

taskCatalog.title: Handle your vet
taskCatalog.desc: Update your address if staying. If switching, request vaccination records, lab results, and any chronic-care notes for your new vet.
taskCatalog.tips: Get the rabies certificate separately — boarding facilities require it on-site.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Without records, boarding kennels and ER vets may turn you away.

insiderItems: Records emailed to you or straight to the new vet — one call. Refill pet meds before you leave.

Update the address on the MICROCHIP registry — the chip company, not the vet. A found pet scanned at a shelter routes to whatever address is in that registry. The chip number is on your vet paperwork.

taskCatalog.title: Forward your mail
taskCatalog.desc: Keep important mail from landing at your old address: file through the official USPS change-of-address page and verify the start date and household members.
taskCatalog.tips: Marketing mail and magazines don't forward — update senders directly.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Anything sent to your old address — bills, tax docs, checks — vanishes.

content.reframe: Ten minutes, $1.10, done. The failure isn't forgetting — it's the fake sites and the late filing.
insiderItems: The only real site is movers.usps.com. Lookalike sites charge $40–80 for the same $1.10 service and take your identity data with it. If the URL isn't movers.usps.com, close the tab.
Forwarding takes 7–10 days to activate. File it a week before the move, not the day the truck comes — a late filing means two weeks of mail landing at the old place.

taskCatalog.title: Request your time off
taskCatalog.desc: Request 2-3 days minimum: one for packing, moving day, and one to recover. Submit at least four weeks ahead.
taskCatalog.tips: Block the day after move day — unpacking always runs longer than expected.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Without time off, you'll be answering Slack with a couch on your back.

content.reframe: Three days: one to finish packing, move day, one to unpack. Request it four-plus weeks out, before the calendar fills.
insiderItems: Take only move day and you're answering work messages with a couch on your back, then starting your first day back living out of boxes.

taskCatalog.title: Cancel your utilities
taskCatalog.desc: Schedule shutoffs for electric, gas, water, sewer, and trash. Set the date for the day after you move out, not the day of.
taskCatalog.tips: Give them your forwarding address — credit refunds arrive by mail.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Utilities running in your name after move-out keep billing you.

content.reframe: Stop date = the day AFTER move-out. The overlap costs a couple dollars; the gap costs cold showers and a fridge of spoiled food.
insiderItems: Expect a deposit or credit check at the new address — a 'letter of credit' from your old utility usually waives it.
Trash and recycling are set by address, not choice — ask the same call who handles pickup at the new place.

taskCatalog.title: Set up new utilities
taskCatalog.desc: Call electric, gas, water, and trash providers 2-3 weeks ahead. Schedule activation the day before you arrive — overlap beats outage.
taskCatalog.tips: Get a 'letter of credit' from your old utility — waives the deposit.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Arriving at a dark, waterless house ruins your first night.

content.reframe: Start date = the day BEFORE move-in. The overlap costs a couple dollars; the gap costs cold showers and spoiled food.
insiderItems: Expect a deposit or credit check at the new address — a 'letter of credit' from your old utility usually waives it.
Trash and recycling are set by address, not choice — ask the same call who handles pickup at the new place.

taskCatalog.title: Transfer your utilities
taskCatalog.desc: Call each provider 1-2 weeks out. Schedule the new address active a day before, the old address shutoff a day after.
taskCatalog.tips: Same provider = no new deposit, no credit check, no setup fee.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Without overlap, you'll lose water mid-clean or power mid-move.

content.reframe: Start the new address the day BEFORE move-in, stop the old the day AFTER move-out. Same provider both ends — one call handles both.
insiderItems: Expect a deposit or credit check at the new address — a 'letter of credit' from your old utility usually waives it.
Trash and recycling are set by address, not choice — ask the same call who handles pickup at the new place.

taskCatalog.title: Update your child's school
taskCatalog.desc: Submit your new address with proof of residency. Update emergency contacts, transportation requests, and pickup authorizations the same day.
taskCatalog.tips: Bus zones change at the address level — confirm yours immediately.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: An old address can drop your kid from the bus route overnight.

content.reframe: The failure is a kid who can't start on day one because the records didn't.
insiderItems: Request records before the last day of school — summer offices run skeleton crews and requests sit for weeks.
Residency proof is the lease or a utility bill, not your license. Get utilities in your name first.
IEP or 504? Hand-carry the FULL evaluation file yourself. It's the one set of records you never trust to the mail.

taskCatalog.title: Find your new daycare
taskCatalog.desc: Get on multiple waitlists immediately — infant care can take 12-24 months. Tour in person and ask about ratios, licensing, and turnover.
taskCatalog.tips: Send a handwritten thank-you after touring — directors remember you.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Waitlists can outlast your move date by a full year.

content.reframe: Daycare is a supply problem — waitlists run in MONTHS, which is why this fires earlier than feels reasonable.
insiderItems: Join 2–3 waitlists. The $25–100 fees aren't waste — they're insurance on your start date.
Ask every center: licensing, ratios, current waitlist length, and what immunization and physical forms they need on file before day one.

ask: Are you licensed, and what are your ratios?
How long is the waitlist right now?
What immunization and physical paperwork do you need before the first day?
get: A spot on the waitlist, in writing.

taskCatalog.title: Update your daycare
taskCatalog.desc: Email the director with your new address, updated emergency contacts, and any drop-off or pickup time changes.
taskCatalog.tips: Update authorized pickup list in writing — verbal changes don't stick.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Outdated emergency contacts can block pickup if your child gets hurt.

content.reframe: Daycare is a supply problem — waitlists run in MONTHS, which is why this fires earlier than feels reasonable.
insiderItems: Join 2–3 waitlists. The $25–100 fees aren't waste — they're insurance on your start date.
Ask every center: licensing, ratios, current waitlist length, and what immunization and physical forms they need on file before day one.

ask: Are you licensed, and what are your ratios?
How long is the waitlist right now?
What immunization and physical paperwork do you need before the first day?
get: A spot on the waitlist, in writing.

taskCatalog.title: Transfer your pharmacy
taskCatalog.desc: Call the new pharmacy with your old pharmacy's name and number — they handle the transfer in minutes for chain stores.
taskCatalog.tips: Controlled prescriptions don't transfer — get a new one from your doctor.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Running out mid-move means an urgent care visit just to refill.

content.reframe: The NEW pharmacy does the work — give them the old pharmacy's name and your med list, they pull everything over.
insiderItems: Refill everything the week BEFORE the move. Never count pills during move week.
Some controlled prescriptions can't transfer at all — they need a fresh script. If any of yours are, ask your doctor before you leave town, not the pharmacist after.

taskCatalog.title: Update your auto insurance
taskCatalog.desc: Notify your insurer with the new address before move day. Premiums shift by ZIP code — sometimes by hundreds per year.
taskCatalog.tips: Get three new quotes the same day — ZIP changes are perfect leverage.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Wrong address on file can void your coverage in a claim.

content.reframe: Your address is a rating factor — the price resets when you move, in either direction.
insiderItems: Before you switch anywhere, make your current company re-quote you at the NEW address as if you were a new customer. Loyalty pricing is real and it works against you.

taskCatalog.title: End-date your condo insurance
taskCatalog.desc: Call your insurer with your move-out date. Schedule cancellation for the day after closing or possession transfer to avoid coverage gaps.
taskCatalog.tips: Ask for a prorated refund — most insurers owe you for unused months.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Cancel too early and a last-day flood becomes your problem alone.

content.reframe: Never cancel — end-date. The old policy ends AFTER the new coverage starts.

taskCatalog.title: End-date your renters insurance
taskCatalog.desc: Call your insurer to cancel — most do it online in 5 minutes. Schedule the end date for the day you hand back keys.
taskCatalog.tips: Ask for the unused premium back — you're owed a prorated refund.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Canceling before key return leaves your stuff uninsured during the last load.

content.reframe: Never cancel — end-date. The renters policy ends AFTER your homeowners coverage starts. No lapse, ever.

taskCatalog.title: Set up condo insurance
taskCatalog.desc: Get an HO6 policy effective on closing day. Read the HOA master policy first — it determines whether you need walls-in or full coverage.
taskCatalog.tips: Ask the HOA which master policy type — bare walls, walls-in, or all-in.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: The wrong HO6 leaves your floors and cabinets unprotected after a leak.

content.reframe: Two policies cover a condo: the HOA's master policy and your HO-6. What yours must cover depends entirely on what the master already does — so the master policy declaration comes FIRST. One email to the HOA; everything waits on it.
insiderItems: Ask every agent about LOSS ASSESSMENT coverage — a cheap add-on that pays your share when the HOA splits a big claim across owners. It's the add-on that earns its premium in condo life.

taskCatalog.title: Set up homeowner's insurance
taskCatalog.desc: Lock in coverage 2-3 weeks before closing. Lenders require a paid first year and proof of binder before they'll fund the loan.
taskCatalog.tips: Quote at least three insurers — premiums vary 30%+ for identical coverage.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Without an active binder at closing, the deal stalls and your move with it.

content.reframe: This runs on the CLOSING timeline, not the move timeline — your lender won't close without insurance bound, 3–4 weeks ahead.
insiderItems: Don't wait until closing week. Roof age, the property's claims history, and flood or fire zones can make a home harder to insure than you expect — and a surprise there delays your closing.
Flood insurance is a SEPARATE policy, not an add-on. If the lender says flood zone, that's a second policy.
First year usually pays at closing through escrow — expect it on the closing statement, not a monthly bill.
Get the bundle price with your auto policy from every company you quote — it's one of the few discounts that's consistently real.

taskCatalog.title: Set up renter's insurance
taskCatalog.desc: Protect your belongings and satisfy lease requirements: compare current coverage and terms from licensed insurers, then bind a policy for move-in day.
taskCatalog.tips: Bundle with auto insurance — usually saves 5-15% on both.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: One pipe burst can wipe out your belongings without coverage.

content.reframe: If your new building requires it, this blocks key pickup. Ten minutes online, effective your move-in date.

taskCatalog.title: Transfer your condo insurance
taskCatalog.desc: Call your insurer 2-3 weeks ahead with the new address. Verify the new HOA master policy type — coverage needs may shift.
taskCatalog.tips: Different HOAs = different coverage needs — re-quote, don't just transfer.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: An assumed transfer can leave gaps your old policy covered automatically.

content.reframe: Two policies cover a condo: the HOA's master policy and your HO-6. What yours must cover depends entirely on what the master already does — so the master policy declaration comes FIRST. One email to the HOA; everything waits on it.
insiderItems: Ask every agent about LOSS ASSESSMENT coverage — a cheap add-on that pays your share when the HOA splits a big claim across owners. It's the add-on that earns its premium in condo life.

taskCatalog.title: Transfer homeowner's insurance
taskCatalog.desc: Call your insurer 3-4 weeks before closing. Premiums shift with location, age, square footage, and roof — get a new quote either way.
taskCatalog.tips: Re-quote three insurers — transfers rarely beat fresh-quote pricing.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: A 'transfer' often hides a premium increase you'd catch by shopping.

content.reframe: This runs on the CLOSING timeline, not the move timeline — your lender won't close without insurance bound, 3–4 weeks ahead.
insiderItems: Don't wait until closing week. Roof age, the property's claims history, and flood or fire zones can make a home harder to insure than you expect — and a surprise there delays your closing.
Flood insurance is a SEPARATE policy, not an add-on. If the lender says flood zone, that's a second policy.
First year usually pays at closing through escrow — expect it on the closing statement, not a monthly bill.
Get the bundle price with your auto policy from every company you quote — it's one of the few discounts that's consistently real.

taskCatalog.title: Transfer renter's insurance
taskCatalog.desc: Call your insurer with the new address 1-2 weeks ahead. Transferring keeps your claims-free discount and skips the new policy fee.
taskCatalog.tips: Ask for the multi-year loyalty discount — most insurers don't volunteer it.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Restarting fresh resets discounts you've spent years earning.

content.reframe: One call: new address, effective move-in date. Or use the move as the moment to re-shop — renters policies are cheap enough that loyalty never pays.

taskCatalog.title: Scan your home
taskCatalog.desc: Pan your camera slowly across each room. Peezy's AI identifies furniture, appliances, and large items in about 20 seconds per room.
taskCatalog.tips: Open closets and cabinets — Peezy catches what you'd forget to mention.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: An accurate inventory unlocks precise quotes and protects you against damage claims.

taskCatalog.title: Defrost your freezer
taskCatalog.desc: Empty the contents, unplug it, prop the doors open, and lay towels underneath. Plan 24-48 hours before move day.
taskCatalog.tips: After moving, let it sit upright for 4 hours before plugging back in.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Movers won't load a wet or leaking fridge — full stop.

walkthrough: Two days before the move: empty the freezer.
Towels at the base, door propped open.
Move day: pour out the drip tray and wipe it dry.
content.reframe: Skip it and the ice melts in the truck — water through your boxes for the whole drive.

taskCatalog.title: Deep clean the place
taskCatalog.desc: Plan 6+ hours with two people. Hit appliances, baseboards, walls, windows, vents, and cabinets — landlords inspect every one.
taskCatalog.tips: Clean inside the oven and fridge first — they're the top deduction trigger.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: One missed area can cost you hundreds in deposit deductions.

taskCatalog.title: Do the final touch-up
taskCatalog.desc: After everything is out, walk every room, closet, and cabinet. Wipe baseboards, sweep floors, and confirm nothing is left behind.
taskCatalog.tips: Bring a flashlight — corners and closets hide more than you think.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: A forgotten item or dusty corner is exactly what landlords cite.

taskCatalog.title: End-date your homeowners insurance
taskCatalog.desc: Call your insurer once the sale closes. Set the cancellation date for the day after closing — never before.
taskCatalog.tips: Ask for the prepaid premium refund — most owe you for unused months.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Canceling early voids coverage during the final walkthrough and key transfer.

content.reframe: Never cancel — end-date. The old policy ends AFTER the new coverage starts. A lapse of even a day is the gap claims live in.

taskCatalog.title: Update your license address
taskCatalog.desc: Bring your current license and two proofs of new address to the DMV. Most states require updates within 30 days.
taskCatalog.tips: Check your state — many let you update online without an appointment.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: An outdated address can void traffic ticket service and jury duty notices.

insiderItems: Most states let you update the address online in minutes — the trip is only for a new card. Say yes to the voter-registration checkbox while you're in there.

taskCatalog.title: Handle the new-state DMV
taskCatalog.desc: One DMV trip covers it: new license, and vehicle registration if you drive. Most states give you 30 days after the move.
taskCatalog.tips: Request REAL ID — TSA needs a new one in your new state.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Driving past the deadline on an out-of-state license is a moving violation.

insiderItems: Bring TWO proofs of residency — most states want two, and the lease plus a utility bill is the pair that works.
Registering an out-of-state vehicle? Many states require a VIN or safety inspection FIRST, at a separate location. Check before the trip or you'll make it twice.
Say yes to voter registration at the counter — it's one checkbox and it's done.

docs: Two proofs of residency (lease + utility bill)
Title or registration if registering a vehicle

taskCatalog.title: Reserve move-out access
taskCatalog.desc: Lock in truck parking — and the service elevator if your building has one — before move day.
taskCatalog.tips: Reserve two adjacent spots — trucks need ramp clearance too.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: No reserved access means movers burn paid hours hunting for parking.

content.reframe: Email or call the front desk — they book it. One contact, three questions, three failures dead.

ask: Reserve the elevator for the move date and window.
Do movers need a COI? Buildings that require one turn crews away at the door — your mover's office sends it same-day if asked ahead.
Where does the truck park? Unarranged parking is long-carry distance, and hourly crews bill the walk.
get: The COI requirements to forward to your movers.

taskCatalog.title: Reserve move-in access
taskCatalog.desc: Lock in truck parking at the new building — and the service elevator if there is one — before the truck arrives.
taskCatalog.tips: Ask the building to cone off the spot the night before.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: An unreserved elevator is the #1 cause of movers' overtime charges.

content.reframe: Email or call the front desk — they book it. One contact, three questions, three failures dead.

ask: Reserve the elevator for the move date and window.
Do movers need a COI? Buildings that require one turn crews away at the door — your mover's office sends it same-day if asked ahead.
Where does the truck park? Unarranged parking is long-carry distance, and hourly crews bill the walk.
get: The COI requirements to forward to your movers.

taskCatalog.title: Photograph the old place
taskCatalog.desc: Photograph the empty unit, return every key and fob, and keep the record — your deposit's evidence file.
taskCatalog.tips: Shoot video too — it captures context photos miss.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Without proof, deductions are your word against theirs.

content.reframe: Sequence is everything: empty → clean → photograph → keys. Deposit disputes are photo wars — the landlord has theirs.
insiderItems: Wide shot of every room, inside the oven and fridge, closets open, close-ups of damage that was already there. Your camera roll timestamps everything.
Shoot the electric and gas meters on the way out — kills any final-bill dispute.

taskCatalog.title: Handle the school transfer
taskCatalog.desc: Notify the current school, request records, and start enrollment at the new district — one parental job, one card.
taskCatalog.tips: Many districts let you start enrollment paperwork online before you arrive.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Enrollment gaps cost kids school days.

content.reframe: The failure is a kid who can't start on day one because the records didn't.
insiderItems: Request records before the last day of school — summer offices run skeleton crews and requests sit for weeks.
Residency proof is the lease or a utility bill, not your license. Get utilities in your name first.
IEP or 504? Hand-carry the FULL evaluation file yourself. It's the one set of records you never trust to the mail.

taskCatalog.title: Move your medical records
taskCatalog.desc: One pass across your providers — records requested, addresses updated, transfers started.
taskCatalog.tips: Call the front desk — most offices send records electronically in days.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: New providers can't treat you safely without your history.

content.reframe: Easiest path: your NEW doctor's office requests them — one release form signed there.
insiderItems: Offices can legally take weeks on records requests. Start before you move, not at the first new appointment.

taskCatalog.title: Handle your money accounts
taskCatalog.desc: Banks, cards, brokerages, loans — one pass updates every address so autopay and statements never miss.
taskCatalog.tips: Update before your next statement closes — mismatches trigger fraud alerts.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Outdated info triggers fraud alerts and frozen cards on day one.

insiderItems: Mail forwarding does NOT cover these — banks and brokerages mark statements 'do not forward.' That's why each one is its own task.
Never request a replacement card mid-move. It races your address change and loses.
401(k) and HSA route through your employer's system, not the bank — that one's an HR portal, not a phone call.

taskCatalog.title: Handle your memberships
taskCatalog.desc: Gyms, studios, spas, clubs — cancellations and transfers need 30-day notices. One pass, all of them.
taskCatalog.tips: Check your membership terms — some require 30 days written notice.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Miss a notice window and you pay for a gym you can't visit.

taskCatalog.title: Choose your storage unit

researchPrefs.question: What matters most when you choose storage?
When do you need the unit?
What is your main storage need?

taskCatalog.desc: Avoid sold-out or inconvenient storage: compare current, sourced options near your new place, then confirm availability and terms directly.
taskCatalog.tips: Reserve early, and confirm every promotion and move-in term before paying.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Sold-out units near the new place mean storing across town.

taskCatalog.title: Add your new address
taskCatalog.desc: Your plan is waiting on the destination. Add it and everything downstream unlocks.
taskCatalog.tips: A street address beats a city — distance and deadlines get exact.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Distance, deadlines, and half your tasks depend on where you're headed.

taskCatalog.title: Lock in your move date
taskCatalog.desc: You marked the date flexible. Lock it in — or confirm the estimate — so the plan paces itself right.
taskCatalog.tips: Mid-month weekdays book cheaper movers than month-end weekends.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Every deadline on your plan counts backward from this date.

taskCatalog.title: Lighten the load?
taskCatalog.desc: Move less and lower the packing load: choose what to sell or donate, then use a step-by-step plan for each item.
taskCatalog.tips: Every unsold item becomes a box you pay to move.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Selling and donating both need lead time — the earlier we know, the more it pays.

taskCatalog.title: Need a storage unit?
taskCatalog.desc: Know before move day whether it all fits — and what a unit near you actually costs.
taskCatalog.tips: Units near new builds sell out first — early answers get options.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Waiting until move day can leave only inconvenient or unsuitable options.

taskCatalog.title: Tell us how moving day went
taskCatalog.desc: Protect your own record of moving day: capture arrival, pace, final price, and damage while details are fresh.
taskCatalog.tips: Stick to what happened — arrival, pace, price, and damage.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Fresh facts give you a clear record for reviews, claims, or disputes.

taskCatalog.title: Return or recycle your boxes
taskCatalog.desc: Reduce waste and improve future kit estimates: count what left your home, then choose a local donation, reuse, or recycling option.
taskCatalog.tips: Flatten clean boxes before donation or recycling, and keep wet or damaged cardboard separate.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Returned counts reduce waste and make the next kit estimate sharper.

taskCatalog.title: Give your daycare written notice
taskCatalog.desc: Most daycare contracts require 2–4 weeks written notice — or they keep billing after you're gone.
taskCatalog.tips: Check the contract for the notice clause, then send it dated, in writing.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Miss the notice window and you pay tuition for a spot you no longer use.

taskCatalog.title: Get the HOA master policy declaration
taskCatalog.desc: One email to the HOA (or your realtor). Your condo insurance can't be quoted without it.
taskCatalog.tips: Ask for the 'master policy declaration page' — those exact words.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Your HO-6 coverage depends on what the master policy already covers. Guessing means paying for overlap or leaving a gap.

taskCatalog.title: Return your modem and equipment
taskCatalog.desc: Return the modem and router, get a receipt, photograph it into your notes.
taskCatalog.tips: Unreturned-equipment fees run $100+ and land months later — the receipt photo is the whole defense.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Providers bill for equipment they claim never came back. Your receipt says otherwise.

taskCatalog.title: Truck pickup checklist
taskCatalog.desc: At the counter: confirm the ramp, dolly, and pads are on the reservation. Photograph the fuel gauge and odometer before you drive off.
taskCatalog.tips: The pickup photos are your dispute evidence — take them every time.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Fuel and damage disputes are decided by whoever has photos.

taskCatalog.title: Update your auto insurance
taskCatalog.desc: One call or portal visit: new address, effective your move date. Cross-state, they'll write a new policy for the new state — same call starts it.
taskCatalog.tips: Do this BEFORE any DMV trip — registration needs proof of insurance at the new address.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Your address is a rating factor, and the DMV wants the proof before it wants anything else.

taskCatalog.title: Shop auto insurance at your new address
taskCatalog.desc: Quote 2–3 companies at the new address — and make your current company re-quote you at new-customer rates before you switch.
taskCatalog.tips: New coverage starts BEFORE the old policy ends. No lapse, ever.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: The move resets your price anyway — this is the one moment shopping costs you nothing extra.

taskCatalog.title: Update address with {institution}
taskCatalog.desc: Log in or call, update mailing AND billing address, keep the confirmation.
taskCatalog.tips: Mail forwarding does NOT cover this — banks mark statements 'do not forward.' And never request a replacement card mid-move.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Financial mail doesn't follow you. Each institution has to hear it from you directly.

taskCatalog.title: Update your voter registration
taskCatalog.desc: vote.gov, your state, two minutes online.
taskCatalog.tips: States close registration weeks before an election — if one's coming, this moves early.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Your registration doesn't move with you.

taskCatalog.title: Handle your vet
taskCatalog.desc: Got pets? Two quick things protect them in the move — records and the microchip registry.
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Without records, boarding kennels and ER vets may turn you away.

taskCatalog.whyNeeded: Running out mid-move means an urgent care visit just to refill.

taskCatalog.desc: Seeing any specialists you'll need records from — cardiologist, OB, derm, anyone?
taskCatalog.whyNeeded: New providers can't treat you safely without your history.

steps.body: Block the day after move day — unpacking always runs longer than expected. Without time off, you'll be answering Slack with a couch on your back.
Buy 20% more small boxes than you think — books, kitchen stuff, and bathroom items fill them fast. Big boxes get dangerously heavy.
A freezer that's not fully defrosted leaks across the moving truck floor and ruins cardboard boxes on contact.
Pack a 'last bag' with cleaning supplies — load it onto the truck last. Once boxes are sealed, finding a sponge becomes a 30-minute hunt.
Clean inside the oven and fridge first — they're the top deduction trigger. One missed area can cost you hundreds in deposit deductions.
Bring a flashlight — corners and closets hide more than you think. A forgotten item or dusty corner is exactly what landlords cite.
Set up mail forwarding through the official USPS change-of-address page. Choose the start date, verify who is moving, and update any senders USPS does not cover.
Contact the registrar with your new address and proof of residency. Also update emergency contacts, bus routes, and after-school programs.
Give your current daycare 2-4 weeks written notice. Request copies of developmental records and immunization history. Ask for recommendations near your new address.

Start calling providers now — waitlists for infant and toddler spots can be 3-6 months. Contact at least 5 providers near your new address, ask about openings for your child's age group, and get on every waitlist. It costs nothing and saves you from scrambling after the move.

Check your state — many let you update online without an appointment. An outdated address can void traffic ticket service and jury duty notices.
Request REAL ID — TSA needs a new one in your new state. Driving past the deadline on an out-of-state license is a moving violation.
Update auto insurance first — DMV won't register without it. Outdated tags risk tickets, towing, and insurance denial in a crash.
